concepts.title: Quadratics, Matrices, P&C, Binomial
concepts.description: Quadratics, Matrices, P&C, Binomial — part of the chapter on Algebra.
key_ideas: Core principles of quadratics, matrices, p&c, binomial
Step-by-step problem solving for quadratics, matrices, p&c, binomial
Real-world applications of quadratics, matrices, p&c, binomial

concepts.title: Sets, Relations, and Functions
concepts.description: Foundational concepts involving set theory, mapping logic, and the definitions of relations and functions essential for calculus and higher algebra.
key_ideas: Set operations and Venn diagrams
Types of relations: Reflexive, Symmetric, Transitive, Equivalence
Function definitions: Domain, Codomain, Range
Classification of functions: One-to-one, Onto, Inverse functions

concepts.title: Sequences and Series
concepts.description: Study of numerical progressions, summation techniques, and inequalities relating to means, forming the basis for discrete analysis.
key_ideas: Arithmetic (AP), Geometric (GP), and Harmonic (HP) Progressions
Arithmetico-Geometric Series (AGP)
AM-GM-HM Inequalities
Telescoping series and Sigma notation

concepts.title: Complex Numbers
concepts.description: Analysis of the complex number system, including algebraic properties and their geometric interpretations in the Argand plane.
key_ideas: Algebra of complex numbers and conjugate properties
Modulus, Argument, and Polar/Euler forms
Cube roots of unity and De Moivre's Theorem
Geometry of complex numbers (Rotation, Locus)

concepts.title: Probability
concepts.description: Mathematical framework for quantifying uncertainty, leveraging counting principles to solve problems involving random events.
key_ideas: Axiomatic probability and addition theorems
Conditional probability and Independent events
Total Probability Theorem and Bayes' Theorem
Bernoulli trials and Binomial distribution

concepts.title: Mathematical Reasoning
concepts.description: Introduction to logic, statement validity, and logical connectives used to construct mathematical arguments.
key_ideas: Statements and logical connectives (AND, OR, NOT)
Implications: Converse, Inverse, Contrapositive
Tautology and Fallacy
Algebra of statements

concepts.title: Limits, Differentiation, Integration, DEs
concepts.description: Limits, Differentiation, Integration, DEs — part of the chapter on Calculus.
key_ideas: Core principles of limits, differentiation, integration, des
Step-by-step problem solving for limits, differentiation, integration, des
Real-world applications of limits, differentiation, integration, des

concepts.title: Functions and Graphical Transformations
concepts.description: Foundational study of function types, their domains, ranges, and graphical behaviors including composite and inverse functions.
key_ideas: Domain and Range calculation
One-one (Injective) and Onto (Surjective) mapping
Composite and Inverse functions
Graphical transformations (shifting, scaling, reflection)

concepts.title: Continuity and Differentiability
concepts.description: Analysis of function behavior at specific points to determine if a graph is unbroken or smooth, focusing on critical points and piecewise functions.
key_ideas: Types of Discontinuity (Removable, Jump, Infinite)
Intermediate Value Theorem
Relationship between Continuity and Differentiability
Differentiability of modulus and piecewise functions

concepts.title: Applications of Derivatives (AOD)
concepts.description: Utilizing derivatives to analyze the shape of curves, rates of change, and optimization problems.
key_ideas: Tangents and Normals
Monotonicity (Increasing and Decreasing functions)
Maxima and Minima (First and Second Derivative Tests)
Mean Value Theorems (Rolle's and Lagrange's)

concepts.title: Properties of Definite Integrals
concepts.description: Advanced techniques for evaluating definite integrals using symmetry, periodicity, and specific integral properties rather than finding antiderivatives.
key_ideas: King's and Queen's Properties
Leibniz Rule (Differentiation under the integral sign)
Integrals of periodic and odd/even functions
Estimation of Definite Integrals (Inequalities)

concepts.title: Area Under Curves (Quadrature)
concepts.description: Geometric application of definite integration to calculate the area bounded by curves, lines, and axes.
key_ideas: Area between two curves
Area involving modulus functions
Curve tracing for area determination
Variable integration limits

concepts.title: Methods for Solving Differential Equations
concepts.description: Systematic approaches to finding general and particular solutions for first-order differential equations.
key_ideas: Variable Separation method
Homogeneous Differential Equations
Linear Differential Equations (Integrating Factor)
Exact Differential Equations

concepts.title: Lines, Circles, Conics
concepts.description: Lines, Circles, Conics — part of the chapter on Coordinate Geometry.
key_ideas: Core principles of lines, circles, conics
Step-by-step problem solving for lines, circles, conics
Real-world applications of lines, circles, conics

concepts.title: Cartesian System and Locus
concepts.description: Foundational principles of the 2D Cartesian plane, including distance and section formulas, area of polygons, and the mathematical definition of a locus based on geometric conditions.
key_ideas: Distance and Section formulas (internal and external division)
Coordinates of special centers: Centroid, Incenter, Orthocenter, Circumcenter
Step-by-step procedure for finding the equation of a Locus

concepts.title: Transformation of Axes
concepts.description: Techniques to simplify algebraic equations of curves by shifting the origin or rotating the coordinate axes without changing the relative position of points.
key_ideas: Translation of axes (Shifting origin)
Rotation of axes (Removing the xy term)
Invariants under transformation

concepts.title: Pair of Straight Lines
concepts.description: Study of the joint equation of two lines passing through the origin (homogeneous) and general equations representing two lines, including conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity.
key_ideas: Homogeneous equation of second degree: ax² + 2hxy + by² = 0
Angle between pair of lines and condition for perpendicularity (a+b=0)
Equation of angle bisectors
General equation of second degree representing a pair of lines (Δ = 0)

concepts.title: Tangents and Normals (General Theory)
concepts.description: Unified approach to finding equations of tangents and normals for circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas using slope forms, point forms, and parametric forms.
key_ideas: Condition of tangency for line y = mx + c against various conics
Equation of tangent at a point (T = 0)
Parametric coordinates and parametric equations of tangents
Properties of normals for specific conics

concepts.title: Interaction of Points and Conics
concepts.description: Advanced geometric properties arising from the interaction of external points with conic sections, including chords of contact, director circles, and the concept of families of curves.
key_ideas: Position of a point relative to a conic (S1 notation)
Equation of Chord of Contact (T = 0)
Equation of Chord with a given midpoint (T = S1)
Director Circle properties (Locus of intersection of perpendicular tangents)
Family of lines and circles (S + λL = 0)

concepts.title: Vectors, Lines and Planes in 3D
concepts.description: Vectors, Lines and Planes in 3D — part of the chapter on Vectors and 3D Geometry.
key_ideas: Core principles of vectors, lines and planes in 3d
Step-by-step problem solving for vectors, lines and planes in 3d
Real-world applications of vectors, lines and planes in 3d

concepts.title: Scalar and Vector Products
concepts.description: Exploration of the Dot (Scalar) and Cross (Vector) products, including their geometric interpretations, properties, and applications in physics and geometry.
key_ideas: Scalar product for finding angles and projection of one vector onto another
Vector product for finding perpendicular vectors and area of triangles/parallelograms
Conditions for orthogonality and collinearity
Lagrange's Identity relating dot and cross products

concepts.title: Scalar and Vector Triple Products
concepts.description: Detailed study of Scalar Triple Product (STP) and Vector Triple Product (VTP), focusing on expansion formulas and geometric significance involving volumes and coplanarity.
key_ideas: Scalar Triple Product (Box Product) representing the volume of a parallelepiped
Condition for coplanarity of three vectors (STP = 0)
Vector Triple Product expansion formula: a x (b x c) = (a.c)b - (a.b)c
Reciprocal system of vectors

concepts.title: Skew Lines and Shortest Distance
concepts.description: Analysis of lines in 3D space that are neither parallel nor intersecting (skew lines), and the calculation of the shortest distance between them.
key_ideas: Definition and identification of skew lines versus intersecting lines
Formula for shortest distance between two skew lines using vector methods
Distance between two parallel lines
Finding the equation of the line of shortest distance

concepts.title: Intersection of Planes and Family of Planes
concepts.description: Advanced study of the relationship between multiple planes, including angles between planes, lines of intersection, and the equation of a plane passing through the intersection of two others.
key_ideas: Angle between two planes and angle between a line and a plane
Equation of a plane passing through the intersection of two planes (Family of Planes)
Equation of angle bisectors of two planes
Image and foot of perpendicular of a point with respect to a plane

concepts.title: Trigonometric Equations and Inverse Trig
concepts.description: Trigonometric Equations and Inverse Trig — part of the chapter on Trigonometry.
key_ideas: Core principles of trigonometric equations and inverse trig
Step-by-step problem solving for trigonometric equations and inverse trig
Real-world applications of trigonometric equations and inverse trig

concepts.title: Compound Angles and Transformation Formulas
concepts.description: Fundamental trigonometric operations involving the sum and difference of angles, and techniques to transform products of trigonometric functions into sums and vice versa.
key_ideas: Addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent
Transformation of product to sum and sum to product
Trigonometric ratios of allied angles

concepts.title: Multiple and Sub-multiple Angles
concepts.description: Analysis of trigonometric ratios for angles that are multiples (2A, 3A) or sub-multiples (A/2) of a given angle, including derivation of key identities used in calculus.
key_ideas: Double angle and triple angle formulas
Half-angle formulas in terms of semi-perimeter
Expressing sin, cos, and tan in terms of tan(A/2)

concepts.title: Periodicity and Extremum Values
concepts.description: Study of the periodic nature of trigonometric functions and methods to determine the maximum and minimum values of trigonometric expressions.
key_ideas: Finding the period of composite trigonometric functions
Range of the expression a*sin(x) + b*cos(x)
Using AM-GM inequality for trigonometric extrema

concepts.title: Properties of Triangles (Sine and Cosine Rules)
concepts.description: Application of trigonometry to relate the sides and angles of a triangle, forming the basis for solving general triangles.
key_ideas: Sine Rule and Cosine Rule
Projection Formula
Napier's Analogy (Tangent Rule)

concepts.title: Solution of Triangles: Circles and Radii
concepts.description: Advanced study of the geometric centers of triangles and their associated circles (incircle, circumcircle, excircles) using trigonometric formulas.
key_ideas: Formulas for Inradius (r) and Circumradius (R)
Properties of Ex-radii and Ex-centers
Relations between Orthocenter, Centroid, and Circumcenter

concepts.title: Heights and Distances
concepts.description: Practical application of trigonometry to determine vertical heights and horizontal distances in real-world scenarios involving angles of elevation and depression.
key_ideas: Angle of Elevation and Depression
Solving problems in two and three dimensions
North-East-South-West bearing problems

concepts.title: Probability and Distributions
concepts.description: Probability and Distributions — part of the chapter on Probability and Statistics.
key_ideas: Core principles of probability and distributions
Step-by-step problem solving for probability and distributions
Real-world applications of probability and distributions

concepts.title: Axiomatic Probability and Algebra of Events
concepts.description: Introduction to the set-theoretic approach to probability, including sample spaces, event types, and the addition theorems.
key_ideas: Sample space and event definitions (mutually exclusive, exhaustive)
Axiomatic definition of probability
Addition theorem for two and three events
Probability of 'at least one' or 'exactly one' event

concepts.title: Conditional Probability and Independence
concepts.description: Analysis of events occurring under specific conditions and the mathematical definition of independent events.
key_ideas: Definition and formula of conditional probability
Multiplication theorem of probability
Pairwise vs. mutual independence of events
Solving problems involving replacement vs. non-replacement

concepts.title: Total Probability and Bayes' Theorem
concepts.description: Advanced probabilistic reasoning involving the Law of Total Probability and calculating inverse probabilities using Bayes' Theorem.
key_ideas: Partition of a sample space
Theorem of Total Probability
Bayes' Theorem for inverse probability
Applications in diagnostic tests and cause-effect analysis

concepts.title: Bernoulli Trials and Binomial Distribution
concepts.description: Study of repeated independent trials with binary outcomes and the resulting probability distribution.
key_ideas: Conditions for Bernoulli trials
Probability mass function of Binomial Distribution
Calculation of mean and variance for Binomial Distribution
Recurrence relation for binomial probabilities

concepts.title: Statistics: Measures of Dispersion
concepts.description: Statistical analysis of data spread, focusing on variance and standard deviation for grouped and ungrouped data.
key_ideas: Mean deviation about mean and median
Variance and Standard Deviation formulas
Shortcut methods for calculation (Step-Deviation)
Coefficient of variation and analysis of frequency distributions
